summary: A typed block in a text body (comment, ask, message, reply) is drawn as the document draws it: the headless engine gains a renderBlock option (as lib.ts has) through which markdown-engine draws renderTypedBlock for a callout and the AskBlockView shell for an ask; useRenderedMarkdown portals the document's read-only AskBlockCard into the shell's slots through a React context app.tsx provides (breaking the MarkdownBody import cycle); server-owned attributes are reset to defaults on parse so a comment cannot forge an outcome; the typed-block and card styles move from .dispatch-doc to :is(.dispatch-doc, .dispatch-markdown).

tasks.title: Red browser test first
tasks.detail: Two tests on /issues/<KEY>/conversation: a comment's callout shows [data-proof-block-name]=callout, [data-proof-block-badge]=warning (filled background), [data-proof-block-title]=Read this, header height <= 40; a comment's ask block shows [data-dispatch-ask-pill=high] 'High', 'Decision', option rows [data-dispatch-ask-record] with A and B, the source [data-proof-block-content] > ul hidden, border-left-width 4px. Run at the unchanged base: `cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- e2e/text-typed-blocks.e2e.ts --project chromium --project iphone`, expected 4 failed; quote on the PR.

Type-only prosemirror-model imports; no milkdown values. AskBlockView.applyShell uses askBlockShell. No behaviour change in the editors.

findings.finding: 1. 'Shows its card' has two readings (full read-only AskBlockCard vs static shell); the full card shows server-owned attributes a commenter can forge, and the malformed footer's 're-activates' sentence is false in a comment.
findings.answer: D2 picks the document's read-only card (the spec's 'drawing the document uses'; a frame around the same paragraph and list would not fix the complaint). D3 resets server-owned attributes on parse in the text engine; D4 drops the sentence with a detached prop. A3 tests both.

findings.finding: 2. The styling half has no acceptance and the CSS to move is wider than cited; hiding the source list without rows would lose the options.
findings.answer: Task 5 lists every rule to re-scope and the two to keep document-only; D6 sets data-dispatch-ask-options only where a card mounts; A2 adds box height, badge background, folded list and border assertions in chromium and iphone; screenshots light and dark for the reviewer; styles-css-pin swatch comments kept.

findings.finding: 3. A provider in app.tsx would pull ask-block.ts (milkdown state, picture-view) into the entry chunk.
findings.answer: Task 3 moves the pure drawing to typed-block-drawing.ts with type-only prosemirror-model imports and re-points AskBlockCard; A5 greps the entry chunk for the PluginKey literal.

findings.finding: 4. lib-headless.ts is a copied file with fifteen enumerated edit kinds; HostBlockRenderer is not exported from the headless entry; two doc statements become partly false.
findings.answer: Task 2 adds the sixteenth kind and both counts, exports the type; D8 records why the schema hook beats a serializer override (copy attributes); Task 7 rewords AGENTS.md:291 and :898 and the moved doc comment.

findings.finding: 5. Surfaces in scope are unclear; A1 covers one.
findings.answer: D7: inline bodies, MarkdownPreview and headlines stay one line of text by design. The shared path is proven by MarkdownBody unit tests (Task 6); the e2e reads the Conversation tab's comment body, which renders the full MarkdownBody (ConversationTab.tsx:737).

findings.finding: 6. One test cannot show both halves failing; how the test runs on the parent commit.
findings.answer: Task 1 writes two tests and runs them first against the unchanged base (red-first), so no checkout of the parent is needed; the command and expected 4 failures are named.

findings.finding: 7. The production check is undefined and the e2e suite is destructive against production.
findings.answer: The deployment instructions define the check script; A1c names the exact command, page and routes. Nothing is written to production.

findings.finding: 8. Copy and paste out of a comment changes.
findings.answer: D8: accepted; HTML paste reads only the content hole and keeps data-proof-block-attr-* (the reason for the renderBlock path); a plain-text copy carries what the reader sees.

findings.finding: 9. Linkify and search decorate reach the header.
findings.answer: D8: accepted; a reference in a title becomes a link as in every body, a search hit in a title is highlighted; card slots are empty when those passes run.

findings.finding: 10. Portal lifetime under repaint, streaming and late height.
findings.answer: D9: portals keyed ask-<index>; height lands one commit after the body as DispatchPicture does today.

findings.finding: 11. Nested cards and a second decision id under the editor root.
findings.answer: D10: the text shell carries no data-dispatch-ask-block; nesting a card inside a document's ask footer reply is accepted and bounded by content.

findings.finding: 12. Sibling issues touch the same seam.
findings.answer: Read INFRA-525/527/528/529 specs: 527 and 528 add node drawings in the same renderer, 529 changes unknown-directive reading, 525 may move BlockTypeSchema. Recorded as a textual-conflict risk; whichever lands second resolves it; no shared decision needed. Reported to the architect.

specDepartures.spec: Change: 'The read-only engine draws typed blocks with the drawing the document uses.'
specDepartures.plan: Callouts use the document's drawing as is. An ask block uses the document's read-only card, but in text the engine resets server-owned attributes (state, answered_by, answered_at, selected, answer, invalid, copied_from, copied_from_document) to their defaults, and the card omits the malformed footer sentence 'Fix the block text; the decision re-activates once it parses.'
specDepartures.evidence: block-schema.ts:106-121 parses server-owned attributes from markdown and nothing on the comment path validates them, so the unchanged card would draw 'Answered by <anyone>', ticked rows and a 'Copied from' link a commenter wrote (AskBlockCard.tsx:105-128); no server activates a block in text, so the sentence at AskBlockCard.tsx:136-140 is false there.

risks: INFRA-527/528/529/525 touch markdown-engine.ts, useRenderedMarkdown.tsx, lib-headless.ts or BlockTypeSchema: textual conflicts for whichever lands second.
A pod's Playwright run is about three times slower than CI; give commands at least an hour; webkit and firefox projects run only in CI.
The pod's bun test fails Markdown tests until proof-sdk-upstream's src/ is copied in (INFRA-42 rig note); a rig gap, not a finding.
